en: The Buddha Spoke the Sutra on the Story of the *Tandula* Sesame Oil, translated by Zhu Tanwulan of the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
At that time, the Buddha was staying at Mount Yinsuoduo in the kingdom of Magadha. The Buddha’s son, Rāhula, followed the Buddha.
While staying in the mountains,
Rāhula was disturbed by malevolent spirits while sleeping at night and woke up in alarm.
The next morning, he went to where the Buddha was and paid him homage.
He sat down to one side beneath a tree;
Rāhula rested his cheek upon his hand,
lowered his head, and remained silent and dejected.
The Buddha then asked Rāhula,
"Why do you keep your head bowed, as if in a state of fear?
Rāhula replied, "Yesterday night, while lying down to sleep,"
He was harassed by ghosts and spirits.
The Buddha said to Rāhula:
"In the world, there may be humans who harass other humans."
Either mountain deities harass people,
or spirits by the roads and ditches harass people,
or spirits of those who died a good death harass people.
He came wishing to test the person's mastery of the scriptures and the Way,
fearing that others might not know whether their minds were firm or weak.
The Buddha said to Rāhula:
Receive from me this Buddha-spoken incantation for subduing spirits and ghosts.
Should any spirits or ghosts come to harass you hereafter,
hold fast to these names of the spirits and ghosts.
Speak this with a mind of loving-kindness:

*āpake* | *saṃsaṃke* | *amutas* | *kicike kicike* | *jambhe jambhe* | *kārañje* | *vilambe* | *cīrṇe* | *cīrṇe* | *haṃse haṃse* | *indule* | *sundare* | *phale* | *phale* | *pāyave* | *phale*. The Buddha said: "This is the *Tāntra-sūtra*."
The Buddha therefore composed the *Anityatā-sūtra* for his disciples.
The Buddha told his disciples:
"Those who are in distress should read it."
If spirits or ghosts should happen to come and harass one,
one should maintain a mind of compassion and a mind of pity;
purifying oneself, one should look within at the five viscera and contemplate them.
When the Buddha spoke this sutra,
even the sun and moon might fall to the earth,
but the words of the Buddha would never be otherwise.
Now the Buddha has preached this *Dāntra* Sūtra;
because it has been preached, those beings who intend to come and harass people shall not be able to harass them,
nor shall the mountain deities be able to harass them.
The ghosts and spirits by the roadside ditches may not harass people;
the putrid-dead ghosts and spirits may not harass people;
the well-dead ghosts and spirits may not harass people.
Upon hearing these words, the fire did not burn;
though he ate rice, the poison took no effect;
and though he wished to kill someone, the blade would not strike.
Falling into deep water is a peril of not drowning;
being surrounded by four sons is a peril when traveling through secluded places,
or when traveling through districts, towns, or great kingdoms.
Whether in an assembly, or in the midst of a great gathering,
among the elderly, among companions,
while walking, or while sitting or lying down.
There happened to be a practitioner of sorcery who,
upon reading this sutra, found that his sorcery no longer took effect.
The Buddha then spoke to Rāhula.
He had Rāhula cause all the bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, and laypeople to recite it by heart.
